rationale:
M60/JSD40 (the boundary, one statement per form). The re-export rule is scoped to the clause that WRITES a member name, so this fixture pins the other four forms in one file:

  line 1 `export * as ns from`  - a namespace binding, no member name -> `./m:*` at 0.6, unresolved
  line 2 `export { default as D }` - the member is `default` (what the source module exports), NOT the alias `D` this module exports it under. The edge resolves against the SOURCE module's surface, so `./m:default`; `metadata.exportedAs` carries the alias
  line 3 `export { readFile as read } from "fs"` - the same distinction on a bare (non-relative) module: `fs:readFile` at 1.0, not `fs:read`
  line 4 `export {} from` - an EMPTY clause writes no member name and still takes the dependency -> `./m:*` at 0.6
  line 5 `export { "a-b" as c } from` - ES2022 arbitrary module namespace names: the member is a STRING LITERAL, so the unquoting is part of the contract

The `forbidRelationships` rows are the two spellings the pre-fix `alias ?? name` shape produced (`fs:read`, `./m:D`) and the module-level collapse for a clause that writes members.

expectRelationships.note: namespace binding: no member name is written
the edge is about the member the SOURCE module exports
empty clause: dependency taken, no member named

forbidRelationships.note: pre-fix shape: the ALIAS was used as the target, but the alias is a name in THIS module, not a member of fs
pre-fix shape for a default re-export
the module-level collapse must not fire on a clause that writes a member
nor on one that writes a string-literal member
